title: Sigismunda mourning over the Heart of Guiscardo

phase.label: Last bid as a history painter, 1759

source.label: Sigismunda, Wikipedia: the final and most ambitious of his attempts

highlight.text: It was the final and most ambitious of his attempts to secure for himself a reputation as a history painter.

source.author: Wikipedia contributors
source.title: Sigismunda mourning over the Heart of Guiscardo

work.text: My object was dramatic, and my aim to draw tears from the spectator ; an effect I have often witnessed at a tragedy ; and it therefore struck me that it was worth trying, if a painter could not produce the same effect, and touch the heart through the eye, as the player does through the ear.

source.author: William Hogarth
source.title: Autobiographical notes, in Anecdotes of William Hogarth, Written by Himself

work.text: While Hogarth had expected this work to be acclaimed as a masterpiece of dramatic painting, the work was met with criticism and ridicule.

source.author: Wikipedia contributors
source.title: Sigismunda mourning over the Heart of Guiscardo

moment.text: None of the somber grief, no dignity of suppressed anguish, no involuntary tear, no settled meditation on the fate she meant to meet, no amorous warmth turned holy by despair

source.author: Horace Walpole
source.title: On Hogarth's Sigismunda, quoted in Wikipedia

moment.text: At the present day there is no doubt that [Sigismunda] was not fairly treated in the painter's [lifetime].

matters.text: The chief things that have brought much obloquy on me, are first, the attempting portrait painting; secondly, writing the Analysis of Beauty ; thirdly, painting the picture of Sigismunda ; and fourthly, publishing the first print of the Times.

source.author: William Hogarth
source.title: Autobiographical notes, in Anecdotes of William Hogarth, Written by Himself

matters.text: It is probable that Hogarth modelled her on his wife, Jane.
